The range

Shower heads, rails and twin showers

A shower is made of an outlet and a mixer. This page covers the outlets: the shower head, the shower rail, the arm it hangs from and the hand shower. A twin shower, also called a dual shower, puts an overhead head and a hand shower on one fitting.

Which shower type suits your bathroom?

Shower typeWhat it isSuitsOn this page
Rail showerA hand shower on a sliding railFamilies, as the height adjusts for each person67
Dual or twin showerAn overhead head and a hand shower on one armA rain style shower with a hand shower for rinsing69
Combination showerA full length rail with an overhead rose and a sliding hand pieceOne fitting that does everything81
Fixed head and armAn overhead head on a wall arm or ceiling dropperA clean look with a separate hand shower43 heads, 100 arms and droppers
Hand showerA hand piece on a hook or swivel bracketBaths and compact showers59

Counts are read from the product names on this page.

Pricing

Shower prices

Three end-of-line showers show their price on this site, from $90 to $550: Classic Grand Shower Top Inlet, Classic Shower on Bracket and Luxury Grand 2 in 1 Shower Top Inlet. Each is listed in chrome.

The Millennium and ACL showers show Enquire Now. Add them to your enquiry and we confirm the price in the finish you want.

Types

Rain head, hand shower or 2 in 1

A wide overhead head is often called a rain shower head, because the water falls straight down. A hand shower is better for rinsing hair, washing children and cleaning the shower.

A 2 in 1, dual or combination shower gives you both. Many Millennium hand pieces are described as 3 function, and others as single function.

Inlets

Top inlet or bottom inlet

The inlet is where the water enters the shower. A top inlet shower connects high on the wall, where an old shower arm came out, so it suits a renovation that keeps the existing outlet. A bottom inlet shower connects low, at the base of the rail.

32 showers on this page are named top inlet. Check where your water outlet is before you choose.

Sizes

Finishes and head sizes

Overhead heads in the Millennium dual and combination showers are named by diameter: 200, 250, 300 and 400 mm. A larger head gives wider coverage and needs good water pressure to feel full.

Finishes are chrome, brushed nickel, matte black, gun metal, modern brass and rosa. Round and soft square heads are both listed.

End of line

End-of-line showers and the new ranges

The Classic Grand, Classic Shower on Bracket and Luxury Grand 2 in 1 are end-of-line. They are sold at their current price until they are gone, in chrome only.

The Millennium and ACL showers are supplied to order: tell us the model and finish and we confirm the timing.

Plumbing

Checking your plumbing before you choose

Find out three things: where the water outlet is on the wall, whether you have one outlet or two, and your water pressure. A dual shower with a diverter needs only one outlet. A separate overhead head and hand shower need two.

Choose the mixer with the shower: see shower and bath wall mixers. While the walls are open, plan the floor too, with tiles for your bathroom and floor wastes and grates.

Ratings

WELS rating and warranty

13 showers on this page list a WELS rating in their description, such as 3 stars at 8 to 9 litres a minute. If the shower you like does not list one, ask us to check.

ACL lists a 7 year warranty on many of its shower arms and heads. Ask us for the warranty terms of the shower you choose.

Getting it

Pick-up and delivery

Showroom: 43-45 Bonnrigg Avenue, Bonnyrigg NSW 2177. We are open Monday to Friday 7am to 5pm and Saturday 7am to 3pm. Rails and combination showers come in long boxes, so allow for the length if you are collecting. We deliver across Sydney metro.

Showers are part of the tapware section, with mixers and spouts in the same finishes.

Materials

What the showers are made of

ACL describes many of its shower arms as brass construction, and some of its shower heads as stainless steel. Millennium does not state the material in every description, so ask us for the technical data sheet of the shower you choose.

Care

Descaling a shower head

Hard water leaves scale in the nozzles, which makes the spray uneven. Rub the rubber nozzles with your thumb to break it up, or soak the head in a mix of white vinegar and water and rinse it well.

Wipe coloured finishes with a soft cloth only. Do not use descaling chemicals on matte black, brass or rosa finishes unless the maker allows it.

Showers

Shower questions

What is a twin shower?

A twin shower has two outlets on one fitting: a fixed overhead head and a hand shower. A diverter switches the water between them. It is also called a dual shower.

What size rain shower head is best?

A 250 mm head suits most showers. A 300 mm head gives wider coverage and suits a larger shower with good water pressure. A 200 mm head is a good fit for a compact shower.

What is the difference between top inlet and bottom inlet?

It is where the water enters the shower. A top inlet connects high on the wall, at the old shower arm. A bottom inlet connects at the base of the rail, through a hose or elbow.

How much is a shower rail set?

The end-of-line showers with a price on this site run from $90 to $550. The Millennium and ACL rail showers show Enquire Now and are priced when you enquire.

What WELS rating should a shower have?

A higher star rating uses less water. Several showers on this page list 3 stars at 8 to 9 litres a minute. Ask your plumber or builder whether your project has a water efficiency requirement.

Can I swap a shower head myself?

A shower head that screws onto an existing shower arm can usually be swapped with a spanner and thread tape. Anything that changes the pipework in the wall is work for a licensed plumber.

acceptedAnswer.text: A twin shower has two outlets on one fitting: a fixed overhead head and a hand shower. A diverter switches the water between them. It is also called a dual shower.

mainEntity.name: What size rain shower head is best?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 250 mm head suits most showers. A 300 mm head gives wider coverage and suits a larger shower with good water pressure. A 200 mm head is a good fit for a compact shower.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between top inlet and bottom inlet?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is where the water enters the shower. A top inlet connects high on the wall, at the old shower arm. A bottom inlet connects at the base of the rail, through a hose or elbow.

mainEntity.name: How much is a shower rail set?

acceptedAnswer.text: The end-of-line showers with a price on this site run from $90 to $550. The Millennium and ACL rail showers show Enquire Now and are priced when you enquire.

mainEntity.name: What WELS rating should a shower have?

acceptedAnswer.text: A higher star rating uses less water. Several showers on this page list 3 stars at 8 to 9 litres a minute. Ask your plumber or builder whether your project has a water efficiency requirement.

mainEntity.name: Can I swap a shower head myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: A shower head that screws onto an existing shower arm can usually be swapped with a spanner and thread tape. Anything that changes the pipework in the wall is work for a licensed plumber.
